The dataset consists of 520 expert-validated discharges from the ILW campaigns at JET, with 322 disruptive and 198 non-disruptive shots.
The sequence-based model achieves a cross-validated success rate of 96.2% and a false alarm rate of 8.18% when combined with a mode lock indicator for disruption prediction.
The learned latent space representation is zero-centered and has a spherical shape, likely due to the chosen spherical prior.
The visualization of the latent space reveals two main diverging paths towards the disruptive boundary, corresponding to different physical disruptive paths.
Many false alarms were found to be correlated with labeled precursor events like radiative collapse and impurity accumulation.
The sequence-based model showed a mean warning time of 1.3 seconds on unseen test discharges for the hybrid disruption detector.
The dataset was preprocessed to have a balanced ratio of disruptive to stable states using the T_predisr label.
The model was trained using multi-task learning, with four tasks: disruptivity classification, time-to-boundary regression, state reconstruction, and smooth latent trajectory movements.
The sequence-based model outperformed the state-based model in terms of disruption prediction success rate and false alarm rate.
The latent space visualization shows distinct regions for stable flat-top, stable ramp-down, and disruptive states.
The scattered disruptive tails in the fast disruptive region were found to have a mode lock precursor event.
The stable flat-top region is characterized by the area enclosed by green stars and blue squares in the latent space.
The stable ramp-down operational space is enclosed by the blue squares and blue stars in the latent space.
The transitional region is located between the stable flat-top and disruptive regions in the latent space.
The fast disruptive region corresponds to the shorter branch converging towards the lower right corner of the latent space.
